title: Inactive DSH history
donor_inventory: Full per-task source attribution remains in #647 docs/plans/pr612-split/tasks.json, sections.json and net-diff.json. Donor exports/commands/projection-State hunks belong to tasks 19/28/29 and were not imported; donor resume create/adopt lifecycle change was deliberately NOT ported (no public proof required for task30; main adopt semantics preserved with a read-only identity precheck).
implementation: DSH read-only history/import/preview reads use session/list (root identity + cwd validation), session/projections (authoritative fixed cut) and session/page (fixed throughSeq pagination); missing/invalid baselines fail without falling back to activating session/follow. Typed provider.sessions.preview.get uses an opaque identity/cwd/cut-bound cursor with an optional exact native record window and projected-item offset, preserving oversized and terminal native-page items without server state or key parsing. Scope/window bounds are rejected before native reads; offsets are validated against the bounded projection. Preview wire serialization omits absent turnId without changing stored NativeItem or widening client types. Provider capability plus host method gate the UI. All newest-first pages are reversed together; host generation/epoch and cancellation isolate late replies. Resume retains main adopt semantics with read-only identity precheck. No writer creation, activation, prompt, cancel or native journal mutation from browsing.
acceptance: List/preview/history reads do not start a session or mutate native logs; import/refresh/restart compatibility remains intact. Actual browser + real daemon/native fixture passed complete66-row chronological paging,60-item fixed cut despite history growth, cwd/cursor binding, unchanged running control and zero session/create|follow|prompt|cancel|selectModel|commands/execute|session/new|session/load calls. Installed official DSH readonly smoke passed on owned v4 journal copies with a fresh shipped profile and a nonsecret fixture key; both journals remained byte-identical. Old hosts receive no unsupported requests; old clients keep existing messages.
